text:
Both lesson plans address the core request, but Assistant B’s plan demonstrates greater creativity, historical specificity, and pedagogical variety. It employs three distinct drama techniques (role play, mime, theater) across the three days, each tightly linked to key events of the Opium Wars (e.g., Lin Zexu’s opium destruction, the Arrow Incident, the burning of the Summer Palace). The time allocations are realistic, and each day includes structured reflection, deepening student engagement and understanding. Assistant A’s plan, while formally structured with objectives and assessment, is more generic, repeats similar performance tasks on Days 2 and 3, and lacks the same level of historical detail and technique integration. Therefore, Assistant B provides a more effective and engaging lesson plan.
